narrative:
The model estimated an 86.7% probability that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt, and that high estimate is why your law school application was denied. This is a risk prediction, not a certainty, but it means the decision was based on substantial academic risk rather than a finding that you cannot succeed.

The strongest factor was your third-year class-rank decile: you are in the lowest decile, while accepted students average around the sixth decile. That placed you far below the typical admitted profile and pushed the prediction toward failure. Your first-year decile, also the lowest and far below the accepted average of about six, was the second most influential factor and again increased the predicted risk. Your LSAT score of 28, compared with an accepted-student average of about 37, was the third most important factor and also pointed toward failure. Gender and race were not used.

To move forward, ask admissions whether the decision can be reviewed or appealed, and request guidance on what would strengthen a future application. Focus on raising your academic record, preparing thoroughly before retaking the LSAT, and speaking with an advisor about a realistic timeline and alternative law-school pathways.
